response.sql:
WITH per_scan_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    crewref,
    scancount,
    gbsize / spanmin AS gb_per_min
  FROM scans
  WHERE gbsize IS NOT NULL AND spanmin IS NOT NULL AND scancount IS NOT NULL AND spanmin != 0
),
operator_aggregates AS (
  SELECT 
    crewref,
    SUM(scancount) AS total_scans,
    AVG(gb_per_min) AS avg_gb_per_min
  FROM per_scan_metrics
  GROUP BY crewref
),
all_operator_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_min) AS global_avg_gb_per_min
  FROM operator_aggregates
),
filtered_operators AS (
  SELECT 
    oa.crewref,
    oa.total_scans,
    oa.avg_gb_per_min,
    oa.avg_gb_per_min - aoa.global_avg_gb_per_min AS margin_above_avg
  FROM operator_aggregates oa
  CROSS JOIN all_operator_avg aoa
  WHERE oa.avg_gb_per_min > aoa.global_avg_gb_per_min
)
SELECT 
  AVG(total_scans) AS avg_total_scans,
  AVG(avg_gb_per_min) AS avg_gb_per_min,
  AVG(margin_above_avg) AS avg_margin_above_global_avg
FROM filtered_operators;

assumptions.assumption: The 'simple average of that figure across all operators' means an unweighted average of each operator's average GB per minute—that is, each operator contributes equally to the global average regardless of how many scans they performed. This is distinguished from a scan-weighted average where operators with more scans carry more influence.

alternatives.interpretation: If 'simple average across all operators' should instead compute the global average as the mean of all scan-level gbsize/spanmin ratios (giving equal weight to scans rather than operators), use: SELECT AVG(gb_per_min) AS global_avg_gb_per_min FROM per_scan_metrics in the all_operator_avg CTE. This would apply if operators with more scans should have proportionally more influence on the threshold.
